text:
incident-bot: [ALERT] Elevated 5xx rate on /v1/chat (us-west) · 9% errors over 5m · kv-prefix miss ratio spike x12. Top offender: tenant-42. Recommended mitigations: tenant qps reduction, disable prefetch for tenant, prefix bypass for correctness. Pager: @mike_oncall paged.

mike_oncall: Acknowledged. I'm on it. Paging SRE and eng. Who's available for quick mitigations?

tess_eng: I can help. I'm seeing a big uptick in prefix misses on kv-shard-7, looks like prefetch fanout from tenant-42 creating high cardinality.

mike_oncall: plan — 1) throttle tenant-42 to 200rps 2) disable prefetch for tenant-42 3) set prefix bypass for correctness on tx-* 4) apply edge rate-limit. I will run commands and report.

jamal_support: I'll draft a brief customer note for tenant-42. They're in prod, high priority. ETA 10m.

mike_oncall: running commands now:

```
# throttle tenant
./infractl tenant-quota set --tenant tenant-42 --qps 200
# disable prefetch for tenant
./infractl prefetch disable --tenant tenant-42
# bypass KV cache for tx-* prefix for correctness
./infractl kv-cache set-bypass --tenant tenant-42 --prefix "tx-*"
```

Tess — can you watch the kv-proxy and prefetch controller?

tess_eng: applied prefetch disable on control plane, rolling to 3 pods. Watching logs: /var/log/prefetch-controller. Initial tail shows reduced fanout requests.

mike_oncall: adding edge RL rule:

```
kubectl -n edge exec rl-controller -- rlctl add --tenant tenant-42 --rate 200 --burst 400
```

incident-bot: Mitigation events recorded: prefetch_disabled (tenant-42), tenant_quota_set (200rps), kv_prefix_bypass (tx-*). Metrics: 5xx -> 3.2% after 2m, prefix-miss ratio down ~6x.

sara_sre: I'll take the next handoff. Handoff notes: mitigations applied as above, monitoring for 30m. If error rate stays <5%, we plan a controlled ramp of qps in +50rps steps with 5m observation windows.

ops_lead: Add rollback commands and document expected latency impact to customers. Jamal — include note that bypass may increase latency and token cost.

jamal_support: Drafted and posted short status to tenant-42 channel: "We've applied temporary throttling and safe-mode cache bypass to mitigate errors. Expect slightly higher latency. We're monitoring and will update in 30 minutes." Pinged account team.

mike_oncall: initial hypothesis: a prefetch misconfiguration created a combinatorial key expansion for tenant-42 leading to extreme fanout and cache thrashing. Collecting prefetch traces and kv read heatmap for confirmation. Opening incident ticket and attaching traces.

tess_eng: collecting heatmap and traces now. Snippet to attach to ticket:

```
# quick grep for hot prefixes
kubectl -n kv logs kv-proxy-7 | jq '.prefix' | sort | uniq -c | sort -nr | head -n 20
```

mike_oncall: leaving handoff to sara_sre in ~15m. If metrics hold, we'll gradually re-enable prefetch behind a limiter like:

```
./infractl prefetch enable --tenant tenant-42 --rate 50/s --burst 100
```

incident-bot: PagerDuty ack recorded. No escalation required. Postmortem owner set: tess_eng.

sara_sre: Taking over monitoring. I'll keep the tenant throttled until we confirm reduced cardinality. If we see regression we'll revert:

```
# revert throttle
./infractl tenant-quota set --tenant tenant-42 --qps 1000
# re-enable prefetch
./infractl prefetch enable --tenant tenant-42
# remove prefix bypass
./infractl kv-cache clear-bypass --tenant tenant-42 --prefix "tx-*"
```

mike_oncall: noted. Thanks all — leaving oncall to sara_sre. I'll continue to help in ticket. :white_check_mark:

ops_lead: After stabilization, schedule a follow-up to add a circuit-breaker to prefetch path and improve telemetry on prefix cardinality so we can detect this earlier.

jamal_support: Customer updated at 10:12 UTC. Will send follow-up when we start ramping.

incident-bot: Incident state: mitigated -> monitoring. Please add any post-incident notes to the ticket.
